text:
maya: heads up — LumenX hit repeated 429s in prod starting ~09:12 UTC, customer reports outages every minute mark

sam: can you paste one of the request_ids + headers? also which region/edge?

maya: request_id=rx-9f3b, region=us-east-1. log snippet:
```
[09:12:01] rx-9f3b POST /v1/generate 200ms 200
[09:12:59] rx-9f3b POST /v1/generate 58ms 429 X-RateLimit-Limit: 3600/tpm, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, Retry-After: 60
[09:13:01] rx-9f3b POST /v1/generate 62ms 429 X-RateLimit-Limit: 60/rpm, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, Retry-After: 60
```

kevin: interesting — headers show both RPM and TPM exhausted. pattern looks like a spike that aligns with minute boundaries (minute-folding). are they doing many short-lived streams/parallel requests?

maya: customer said they have a sync job that fans out ~120 requests at top of minute to warm caches. they expect the platform to absorb short bursts.

anika: two quick notes: 1) our default per-token TPM and per-route RPM combine — burst allowance is limited by token-windowing, 2) minute-aligned cron bursts often fold into the same one-minute bucket -> apparent 429 storm

sam: mitigation options we can propose to customer:
- smooth client-side fanout (stagger + small jitter)
- implement exponential backoff with jitter and respect Retry-After header
- switch heavy sync to the Dedicated plan or request a temporary quota bump while they fix client
- server-side folding: we can enable short burst windows for their org for a controlled time (ops action)

kevin: adding a small code snippet customers can use (node):
```js
// naive smoothing example
const delay = ms => new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, ms));
async function sendBatch(reqs){
  for (let i=0;i<reqs.length;i++){
    // jitter up to 2s to avoid minute boundary spikes
    await delay(Math.floor(Math.random()*2000));
    await fetch('/v1/generate', {method:'POST', body: JSON.stringify(reqs[i])});
  }
}
```

maya: can we enable a short burst allowance for them while they deploy client fix? the customer is high-usage and on a paying plan.

ops-bot: alert auto-created: ratecap-org=lumenx org_id=org_8345 triggered=5050003208 rule=per_minute_ratecap

sam: I'll open an ops ticket for a temporary burst increase + note in billing. kevin — can you draft wording for the change (scope, duration, rollback)?

kevin: yup — propose: +50% minute burst allowance for 2 hours, monitored, auto-revert. will add a tracing tag to measure fold reduction.

anika: also suggest we add a quick KB entry for customers: "Avoid minute-aligned fanout" with sample client code and recommended backoff. this keeps support load down.

maya: customer-side repro plan (what I told them):
1) run a small loadtest script that sends 120 requests aligned to top of minute to our staging org id
2) observe RPM/TMP headers and 429s
3) rerun with 100ms jitter added between requests and confirm no 429s

maya: here's a simple curl loop you can run to repro in staging:
```bash
for i in $(seq 1 120); do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -X POST "https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"x"}' &
done
wait
```

sam: perfect. I'll follow up with ops ticket id OT-6214 and assign on-call. maya — keep me posted on customer rollout, we'll only enable burst if they agree to the mitigation timeline. :thumbsup:

maya: will do. I'll send the jittered client snippet and staging repro steps to their SRE now. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
